title: Values worked out from data: computed

--- order: 4 unit: build introduces: [vue-computed] title: "Values worked out from data: computed" summary: "Work a value out from other data with computed, so it is worked out again whenever that data changes, and see why a plain calculation goes stale." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 6 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "@page.html#explain-start", zoom: 1.4} caption: "computed works a value out again whenever the data it uses changes" clip: - caption: "Two adults, twelve dollars each." - wait: 1000 - caption: "The total is worked out from adults, with computed." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: " const total = computed(() => adults.value * 12);\n", after: "const adults = ref(2);\n"} - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: ", total", after: "return { adults"} - caption: "Show it on the page." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "

Total: ${{ total }}

\n", after: "

\n"} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 600 - caption: "Two adults: 24 dollars." - wait: 600 - click: {selector: "button", preview: true} - expect: {selector: "#app", contains: "Total: $36", preview: true} - caption: "One more adult, and computed works the total out again: 36." - wait: 800 hook: "A basket total, a score out of ten, the number of unread messages: each is worked out from other data, and must never go stale." --- Some values are not data of their own: they are **worked out** from other data. A ticket total comes from the numbers of adults and children. If the numbers change, the total must be worked out again. ```js const total = computed(() => adults.value * 12 + children.value * 5); ``` `computed` takes a little function that works the value out. Vue runs it again whenever `adults` or `children` changes, so `{{ total }}` is always right. `() => …` is a short way to write a function that gives back what follows the arrow. **The hard part:** a plain calculation, `const total = adults.value * 12 + …`, is worked out **once**, when the page starts, and then never again. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict insight: "Predicting the new total makes students say how it is worked out, and that it must be worked out again after each click." check: type: predict q: "You press Adults + twice. What total does the page show?" options: ["$53", "$29: the total was worked out at the start", "$41", "$31"] actual: "$53: four adults at $12 is $48, plus one child at $5. computed works the total out again after each click." ``` The page starts at 2 adults and 1 child: $29. ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 440 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I changed the tickets until the free programme message appeared." } ``` Press **Run** and change the numbers. Watch the total, and the message that appears at $50. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "computed values follow the data they use; a v-if can test a computed value; a plain calculation in setup is worked out once and goes stale." tasks: - check: type: trace text: "Start with 2 adults and 1 child. Fill in the page after each click." table: | | after | adults | children | total ($) | free programme? | | the start | 2 | 1 | 29 | no | | Adults + | [3] | [1] | [41] | [no] | | Children + | [3] | [2] | [46] | [no] | | Adults + | [4] | [2] | [58] | [yes] | explain: "The total is worked out again after every click, and the v-if tests the new total each time." - check: type: question q: "Why is the total a computed and not a ref of its own?" options: ["It is worked out from adults and children, so it should follow them, never be set by hand", "Refs cannot hold numbers", "computed is faster to type", "A ref would show the wrong number at the start"] answer: 0 explain: "A ref of its own would need every button to remember to change it too. A computed cannot go out of step: Vue works it out from the data." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "Clicking Adults + changes the number of adults, but the total stays at $29. There is no error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 14 fault: logic misconception: vue-derived-once explain: "This total is a plain calculation: it is worked out once, at the start, and never again. Wrap it in computed(() => …)." ``` ### Trace the page The total after each click. ### Why computed? Worked out, not set. ### Spot the bug The total goes stale. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "A new computed is one line plus a return and a {{ }}; a computed can hold an if, as long as it returns the value." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 440 } tasks: - hint: - "The number of people is worked out from adults and children." - "`const people = computed(() => adults.value + children.value);` then return it and show `{{ people }}`." expected: page.html#sol-people check: { type: code, text: "Show the number of people, worked out with computed.", rules: { contains: ["people = computed("] } } - hint: - "A computed can have several lines, as long as it returns the value at the end." - "Inside computed(() => { … }): let sum = the old total; if 6 or more people, take 10 away; return sum;" expected: page.html#sol-deal check: { type: code, text: "Groups of 6 or more people get $10 off the total.", rules: { contains: ["- 10"] } } ``` ### Count the people A second computed. ### A group deal An if inside computed. ## Make: a recipe scaler ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: several computed values that all follow one piece of data." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 440 } check: { type: code, text: "Show at least two ingredients, each worked out from the number of pancakes with computed.", rules: { contains: ["= computed("] } } ``` One pancake needs **25 g of flour** and **40 ml of milk**. Show how much of each you need for any number of pancakes, each with `computed`. Add eggs too if you like (one for every four pancakes: `Math.ceil(pancakes.value / 4)`). ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "A quiz page shows twenty question cards, each with a title, choices and a score. What would save repeating the card's code twenty times?" options: ["A card you make once, used twenty times with different data", "A longer v-for", "Twenty computed values", "Copy and paste"] answer: 0 explain: "Next lesson: components. You make a tag of your own once, then use it as often as you like, each copy with its own data." ``` Next: **components**, tags of your own. ```teacher summary: Students predict a ticket total after two clicks, trace the total and a v-if message, find a plain calculation that goes stale, add a people count and a group deal, and make a recipe scaler. time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can work a value out from other data with computed. - I can explain why a plain calculation in setup goes stale. - I can use a computed value on the page and in a v-if. before: > Read the unit primer first. `computed(() => adults.value * 12 + children.value * 5)` gives a value Vue works out again whenever the refs it reads change. On the page it is used like a ref (`{{ total }}`, `v-if="total >= 50"`). The arrow `() =>` is a short function that gives back what follows it; students do not need more about arrow functions than that. The planted bug is the idea the course names as hard: a value **derived** from data must be computed, or it is worked out once when setup runs and then goes stale. The page shows no error. A useful contrast: a ref is data you set; a computed is data you never set, only work out. Prices are invented for the example. running: - "Predict: ask students to say how the total is worked out before they choose." - "Run: ask what makes the free programme message appear and disappear." - "Investigate: trace on paper first, then check by clicking." - "Modify: for the group deal, ask where the if goes (inside the computed) and what it must give back." - "Make: ask which data everything else is worked out from." struggle: Students make the total a ref and update it in every button. Ask "what is the total worked out from?" and "what if someone adds a button and forgets?" stuck: - see: The total never changes. ask: Is it wrapped in computed? fix: const total = computed(() => …); - see: "A red error: computed is not defined." ask: Is computed in the line that takes things from Vue? fix: const { createApp, ref, computed } = Vue; - see: The total shows NaN or [object Object]. ask: Inside computed, did every ref get its .value? fix: adults.value * 12, not adults * 12. - see: A computed with an if shows nothing. ask: Does the function return the value at the end? fix: Finish with return sum; stretch: "Stop the numbers going below 0 (a computed can't do that: change the buttons, or use Math.max). Add a computed message that says how far from $50 the order is." support: Give the people computed written out; students only return and show it. leads: "Next lesson: components with props. Class idea: name three values on a shopping site that are computed (total, item count, delivery cost)." exit: q: Why does a total made with computed stay right, when a plain calculation in setup does not? a: Vue works a computed out again whenever the data it uses changes; a plain calculation runs once, when the page starts. explain: | 1. Two adults, twelve dollars each. 2. The total is worked out from `adults` with `computed`. 3. Show it on the page with `{{ total }}`: two adults, 24 dollars. 4. One more adult, and `computed` works the total out again: 36. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-people step-4#t2: page.html#sol-deal step-5: page.html#sol-make sources: - title: "Vue.js: Computed properties" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/computed.html checked: 2026-10-12 ```
